answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings before it can be verified. A GPU may run separate chains for separate clones, but it cannot shorten the dependency-bound computation within any one chain; each added identity therefore incurs its own time and compute cost. A Wesolowski proof lets a verifier check completion efficiently, while umber, atlas, and ridge identities remain subject to the same physical delay.
